name: Telugu
status: Built from the full Round 2 check of the Telugu IRV (66 books, Nov 2026). Rules confirmed against whole-Bible counts; native-reader review still recommended.

script_and_encoding: No doubled or misplaced vowel signs (ాా, ిె).
No virama or anusvara in an impossible position; no word-final pollu.
No ZWJ/ZWNJ, zero-width or non-breaking spaces unless the project uses them deliberately.
Arabic digits (the edition does not use Telugu digits); no Latin letters in verse text.
Visarga ః is not a colon; no archaic letters (ఱ, ఁ, ౘ, ౙ).
spelling: Aspirate pairs థ/ధ (అర్థం, స్వార్థం, వృథా, యథార్థ, వ్యర్థం, సామర్థ్యం), ట/ఠ, బ/భ, ద/ధ (వృద్ధి, బుద్ధి).
Minority spellings against a strongly dominant form are listed in minority.py and counted live.
sandhi_word_division: Case suffixes joined to the noun (పట్టణంలో, not పట్టణం లో).
Postpositions and auxiliaries by the edition's dominant form (వరకు, కోసం, బట్టి, వల్ల, పాటు; కలిగి ఉండి).
Negative and prohibitive endings joined (చేయవద్దు, విడిచిపెట్టలేని).
grammar_and_case: కి/కు and ని/ను by the stem vowel (మీకు, నీకు, మాకు are correct).
Verb agrees with subject in gender, number, person; human vs non-human plural (వారు/అవి).
Both members of a pair lengthened (…డానికీ …డానికీ; గానీ … గానీ).
Genitive before గురించి/గూర్చి in headings (X గురించి, not Xలు గురించి).
register: Modern standard Telugu; no literary forms (-చున్న-, మరియు, యొక్క, -ము endings, సెలవిచ్చు is accepted).
One form of each pronoun per speaker (నీవు/నువ్వు; వారు/వాళ్ళు).
Consistent honorifics for God and Christ.
punctuation: Curly quotes “ ” and ‘ ’, paired, nested and continued across verses.
No space before punctuation; one space after; no double spaces.
A full stop at the end of every sentence; no full stop in the middle of a poetic sentence.
Numbers: no space after a thousands comma (2,300 not 2, 300).
names_and_terms: Names as in the dominant whole-Bible form: యెరూషలేము, ఐగుప్తు, యెహోవా, షోమ్రోను (OT).
Book names and abbreviations as in BookNames.xml (Acts = అపొ.కా.).

figures_of_speech: Idioms rendered word for word where Telugu needs the sense (e.g. 'gird up the loins').
Rhetorical questions that a Telugu reader may take as real questions — check the expected answer is clear.
Euphemisms (knew = had relations; slept with his fathers = died).
Metonymy and synecdoche (the cup = suffering; flesh = humanity).
Similes kept as similes (like / as → లాగా/వలె), not turned into metaphors, and the reverse.
Passive divine actions ('it was given') — who acts must remain clear.
Kinship and honorific terms (brother, son of) not narrowed or widened.
